writeup_source_quote: Raman (2026) (*white-bear steering*, WBS) showed that a think/don't-think stance direction taken **from WorkspaceBench's own `directed_modulation` family** lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83 after the band

differences.what: Message explicitly admits the injection band coincides exactly with WBS's band, undercutting the band-location novelty claim more directly than the write-up does.
differences.message_quote: it lands on 20–24, same as WBS, so this is a methodological difference rather than a different result

differences.what: Message reveals that testing WBS's own directed_modulation (DM) direction reproduces the same ~0.78 result, and gives a specific comparison of pair counts (30 vs 35) and effective doses, directly demonstrating overlap with the source's mechanism in a way the write-up never states.
differences.message_quote: I did not reproduce WBS's exact vectors (different data, different dose: my `α=1.39` vs WBS's effective ~0.78, because my `d_l` has different norm and 30 vs 35 pairs), and I confirmed the DM direction gives the same ~0.78 — so the self-written version matches the proven direction without using bench items.

rationale: Both documents credit Raman (2026) / WBS as the direct basis, describing the method as closely mirroring WBS's think/don't-think stance recipe while claiming novelty from being bench-free/portable and from locating the band via a separation-velocity (CAZ) scan rather than fixing it a priori. The message goes further than the write-up in admitting overlap: it explicitly notes the injected band lands on the identical layers as WBS's and reports having directly tested WBS's own directed_modulation direction, finding it gives the same ~0.78 result (plus a pair-count comparison, 30 vs 35), details and admissions absent from the write-up's more guarded framing.
